key_insight: A 9B decision foundation model fine-tuned with QLoRA can classify 24 diseases from symptoms with high accuracy while avoiding autoregressive text generation.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support faster symptom-based triage with interpretable, symptom-level evidence, but it is a research model rather than a clinical decision tool.
method: Adapted Clef-Flash (Qwen3.5 backbone) using 4-bit QLoRA with differential learning rates
Trained on a stratified 960-case training split and evaluated on 240 test cases
Used leave-one-symptom-out counterfactuals to test which symptom phrases most influenced predictions
evidence_signal: On Symptom2Disease, the model reached 95.42% accuracy and 0.9551 macro F1, outperforming ClinicalBERT and zero-shot baselines while running in under 80 ms per record.
watch_item: Performance and explanation quality were shown on a benchmark dataset, so real-world clinical use would need external validation, safety review, and robustness testing.
paper_title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models
